summary: US-023a: A seat map can be marked orphan-preventing (setting only, nothing enforces it yet)
description:
**First of four slices carved out of TKT-175** when its plan showed the ticket to be ~50 files across five services. The architecture is decided — see TKT-175's `kind=plan-final`.

Ships the **decision** and the **setting**, and nothing that acts on either.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] **ADR-041** records the arbitration decision: geometry fetched once at provisioning for the exact immutable published version (ADR-029), projected into inventory, decided under the pool lock. It states why a claim-path catalog call (ADR-010), a new `seat_map.published` subscription, and a commerce pre-check were each rejected — the last because an advisory check cannot satisfy a contention AC.
- [ ] `seat_maps` gains `orphan_prevention_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`; a guarded Down refuses while any map has it on.
- [ ] Catalog's create/read/edit contract carries it. An edit that omits it **inherits the predecessor's value**; an explicit value applies only to the newly minted version (ADR-029: versions are immutable).
- [ ] The back-office venue page can set it on create and on edit.
- [ ] **Nothing reads it.** No event payload changes, no inventory change, no claim behaviour changes. Every existing map and every existing test behaves exactly as before.
- [ ] Spec declared, generated code committed before the gate, browser evidence for the back-office form submission (the repo's rule: an unsubmitted Astro form is unverified).

Quality gates: `make check` green; browser submit evidence.

binding.rule: Local gate: `make check` ... Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate — `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

reference.summary: The architecture, every design decision and the full test plan live in TKT-175's kind=plan and kind=plan-final — read those first, they are not repeated here

governingAdrs.why: A published seat-map version is immutable and an edit mints a new one. That is why the setting is per VERSION and why an edit's omission must inherit rather than reset — and it is the property the whole TKT-175 architecture rests on.
Contract-first: the catalog spec changes and openapi_gen.go plus api-types.gen.ts are committed before the gate.
The migration runs out-of-band as the service's migrate subcommand; the server path never migrates.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ✅ Readiness — PASS

Smallest possible slice: a decision and a flag nobody reads. Its whole risk surface is the migration default and the edit-inheritance rule, both of which are directly testable.

Shaping is inherited: TKT-175's `kind=plan` (gpt-5.6-sol) and `kind=plan-final` (main-agent) decided the architecture, the design, the test plan and the risks before this ticket existed. This child re-scopes delivery, not thinking.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-179

**Selection reason.** First of the four slices TKT-175 was split into, and the only one with no blockers. It carries **ADR-041**, which the other three depend on.

**Branch.** `TKT-179-orphan-prevention-setting`, cut from `origin/main` at `762ee6fc`.

**⚠️ Gate waiver.** Gateless under the standing owner waiver for TKT-35 and its descendants.

**Planning inherited, deliberately.** TKT-175's `kind=plan` (`gpt-5.6-sol`) and `kind=plan-final` (`main-agent`) decided the architecture, the design and the test plan for all four children before this ticket existed. Re-planning each slice would re-litigate a decision already taken and cross-model reviewed. The plan-review that produced the split is the plan for this ticket.

**Stop-condition pre-check.** One additive migration (`seat_maps.orphan_prevention_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, guarded Down) — anticipated by the ticket's own AC. No auth, no money, no CI config. Nothing reads the column, so no behaviour changes anywhere.

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
### Implementation — TKT-179

**Implemented by `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)**, per `config.models.implement`. Branch `TKT-179-orphan-prevention-setting`, commit `268a6ab6`.

#### What shipped

- **`docs/adr/ADR-041-orphan-seat-arbitration.md`** — the decision, with the three rejected shapes and *why* each fails: a claim-path catalog call violates ADR-010, a new `seat_map.published` subscription buys drift, and a commerce pre-check is advisory and so cannot satisfy a contention requirement even in principle. It also fixes the rules the later slices implement — adjacency is `position` order, only *newly* orphaned seats are refused, a row end has one neighbour, liveness is `released_at IS NULL` after `sweepExpired`, and `orphaned_seats` must be a distinct wire code from `seat_taken` because the identities are seats the buyer never requested.
- **Migration `0014`** — `seat_maps.orphan_prevention_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, Down guarded against discarding enabled maps.
- **Store** — the field on `SeatMap`, `SeatMapInput`, and `EditSeatMapInput` (as a **pointer**), carried by create, the geometry read, the venue list and the version history.
- **Contract** — optional on `SeatMapCreate` (default false), **required** on `SeatMap` responses, optional on `SeatMapEdit` where absent means inherit.
- **Back office** — a checkbox on the create-map form.

#### The one design point worth re-reading

`EditSeatMapInput.OrphanPreventionEnabled` is a `*bool`, and the pointer survives the wire-to-store mapping. Collapsing it to a `bool` at the boundary would turn *"the staffer said nothing"* into *"the staffer said off"* — an edit is a geometry change, and silently clearing a revenue rule on every edit is the kind of defect that is invisible until an on-sale ends with a gap-filled house. `COALESCE($3, orphan_prevention_enabled)` in the version-copy is where inheritance actually happens.

#### TDD

`TestSeatMapOrphanPreventionSetting` was written first and observed red (`SeatMap has no field or method OrphanPreventionEnabled`). `TestEditSeatMapInheritsOrphanPrevention` covers the three cases that matter: omitted inherits, explicit applies to the new version, and the predecessor is untouched (ADR-029).

**The contract change also proved itself**: making the field required on responses broke the back-office test fixture at compile time rather than letting it pass with a silent default. That is ADR-028's discipline reaching TypeScript.

#### Nothing reads it

No event payload changed, no inventory code changed, no claim behaviour changed. The schema-4 golden is untouched. That is the point of the slice.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
### Adversarial code review — TKT-179

**Reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (codex `adversarial-review`), per `config.models.aiReview`. Cross-model check holds.

| Pass | Base | Verdict | Findings |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `origin/main` | needs-attention | 1 medium — **real, fixed** |
| 2 | `268a6ab6` (the fix diff) | **approve** | none |

#### 1-1 [medium] `PublishSeatMap` returned a rule-off map for a rule-on version — FIXED

✅ Verified real. `PublishSeatMap` re-reads the map after publishing, **positionally**, and I had not added the new column to that projection. The returned `SeatMap` therefore carried Go's `false` zero value while the stored row said `true`.

That value is not decorative: it is what `SeatMapPublished` is handed and what the API returns. An enabled map would have published as rule-off — and once TKT-181 puts the flag on the wire, **emitted** as rule-off — while the database said otherwise throughout.

The sharpest part of the finding is this: **the required response field would have passed validation the whole time.** Fail-closed validation checks that a field is *present*, not that it is *true*. Making the field required bought a compile-time break in the back-office fixture and no runtime protection at all against a wrong value.

Fixed in `b0bb3bd0` and **mutation-verified** — restoring the old projection reddens `TestPublishSeatMapCarriesOrphanPrevention`, which also asserts the idempotent re-publish path.

This is exactly the failure mode I pointed the review at (*"a positional scan mismatch is a runtime failure, not a compile error"*), and I still shipped one. Worth recording: knowing the trap and enumerating the sites are different acts.

#### Pass 2 — approve, with the audit I should have done myself

The second pass did not just re-check the fix; it enumerated **every** scan-bearing `seat_maps` query and reported the arity of each:

> *"PublishSeatMap is aligned 10/10 in the correct order. Every other scan-bearing seat_maps query is consistent: performance validation 3/3; create RETURNING 5/5; family resolution 1/1 (three sites); current-version lookup 2/2; edit RETURNING 9/9; pin listing 5/5; section/row/seat writes 1/1, 1/1, 2/2; venue listing 8/8; version listing 9/9; geometry 8/8."*

It also confirmed the fix touches nothing else — status transition, `published_at`, `event_emitted_at`/`needsEmit` and the deterministic event identity are unchanged — and that **no production path now returns a default-false flag a caller might trust**. That last check is the one that matters for TKT-181, which will consume this value.

#### Gate

`make check` green after both commits. Browser evidence re-usable as posted on the PR: the real Astro form submitted with `orphan_prevention=on`, redirect followed, setting read back `true`; unchecked box → `false`.

**No unreviewed hunk.**

<!-- sdlc:stage=po-review kind=summary -->
### PO validation — TKT-179 (self-validated under the waived Gate 4)

Merged `7f6f8be7` (squash of PR #149), branch deleted. `make check` re-run on merged `main` → `EXIT=0`, log clean.

| AC | Met | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **ADR-041** records the decision and the rejected shapes | ✅ | `docs/adr/ADR-041-orphan-seat-arbitration.md`. Names why each alternative fails — a claim-path call breaks ADR-010, a subscription buys drift, a commerce pre-check is advisory and cannot satisfy a contention requirement in principle — and fixes the rules the later slices implement. |
| Per-version column, default false, guarded Down | ✅ | Migration `0014`. `TestSeatMapOrphanPreventionSetting` asserts the default in the struct **and** in the column. |
| Contract carries it; edit inherits unless explicit | ✅ | `TestEditSeatMapInheritsOrphanPrevention`: omitted inherits, explicit applies to the new version, predecessor untouched (ADR-029). |
| Back office can set it | ✅ | Browser: real Astro form submitted with `orphan_prevention=on`, redirect followed, read back `true`; unchecked → `false`. |
| **Nothing reads it** | ✅ | No event payload, no inventory code, no claim behaviour. Schema-4 golden untouched. Every existing test green unmodified. |
| Generated code committed before the gate | ✅ | `check-generate` clean across four gate runs. |

#### The honest part

The review found a defect I had already been told to look for. I pointed it at *"a positional scan mismatch is a runtime failure, not a compile error"* and then shipped exactly one: `PublishSeatMap`'s post-publish read kept the old projection, so an enabled map returned `false` — the value handed to `SeatMapPublished`. Knowing a trap and enumerating the sites are different acts, and only the second one works.

And the required-field discipline gave less than it looked like: **fail-closed validation proves a field is present, never that it is correct.** The response would have validated cleanly while lying.

#### Newly unblocked

**TKT-180** — consumers accept `performance.published` schema 5. It must merge before TKT-181 emits it (ADR-017 §5b′).
